messages.content: 你能計算從地球到一個新發現的距離為4.22光年的外行星，再到另一個距離第一顆外行星6.1光年的外行星，最後再回到距離第二顆外行星5.88光年的地球所需的時間嗎？假設真空中光的速度為299792458公尺/秒。

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years. This is a float type value.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

message.reasoning: We need to compute total travel time: Earth to first exoplanet (4.22 ly), then to second exoplanet (6.1 ly from first?), then back to Earth from second exoplanet (5.88 ly). Actually distances: Earth to first exoplanet: 4.22 ly. Then from first to second: 6.1 ly. Then from second back to Earth: 5.88 ly. Sum distances: 4.22 + 6.1 + 5.88 = 16.2 ly. Compute time: 16.2 light-years / (speed of light). But light-year is defined as distance light travels in one year. So 1 ly = c * 1 year. So time in years = distance in ly. So total time = 16.2 years. But maybe they want in seconds. Use function to compute each segment? The function calculates time given distance in light years. We can call it thrice or sum. Let's use function for each segment. Provide result in years and seconds. Use speed_of_light default. We'll call function for each segment.
